key_insight: A quantum vortex ring in pipe flow develops an energy–momentum spectrum that depends on background flow speed, allowing negative and very large effective masses and suggesting a new route to turbulence onset.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a physics-based way to estimate a critical quantum Reynolds number and identify flow conditions where vortex pairs and turbulence may emerge in superfluid systems.
method: Quantize a classical closed vortex filament using the author’s earlier technique.
Analyze the vortex-ring energy spectrum E(p) as a function of total momentum and background flow velocity v.
Compare a quantum Reynolds-number analogue against the single-vortex critical threshold to predict paired-vortex states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical spectrum analysis showing states with negative and arbitrarily large effective mass, plus a criterion for coupled vortex-pair formation.
watch_item: The conclusions are model-based and depend on the chosen quantization framework, so experimental validation would be needed before using them as design rules.
paper_title: Quantum vortex in a fluid flow: negative effective mass and a novel mechanism for turbulence formation
